limitations: One formal observation per configuration/profile; no confidence interval or randomized run order.

The fixed16-step frame cadence can alias page-growth/control boundaries. Frame distributions are not unbiased per-step latency or stall-frequency estimates; BCT and full native weighted windows remain primary.
Historical v19/v20 have no per-frame thread/runqueue data. Their regression cannot be uniquely attributed to historical OS scheduling or network congestion.

Host CPU covers Python and driver submission; off-CPU includes blocking driver work. GPU stream intervals include host launch gaps and peer waits. These overlapping intervals cannot be added or subtracted into exact wire time.
Independent communication floor is an arrival-skew reference, not an exact decomposition of in-model collective time. Host RDMA counters are not job exclusive.
Component samples are sparse and v22 sampling expanded; only matched calls support historical stage comparisons. Every16th frame remains sampled rather than every step.

Frozen SGLang is not a fresh run: TP16/DP-attention16/EP1, resident weights, different effective prefill chunks, TRT-LLM/FlashInfer kernels and framework CUDA graphs remain unisolated configuration/implementation differences.
Returned-field consistency and real layer parity do not resolve historical strict attention and NaN-tail full-quality failures.
